statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Viet Nam National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) — https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in the Vietnamese alphabet using Latin characters with all appropriate diacritical marks. The name may include letters of the Latin alphabet, digits, and auxiliary symbols provided that a natural Vietnamese reading is retained. A foreign trade name or trademark may be included in parentheses after the Vietnamese-language core name, but must not dominate the registerable name. Names must not be wholly in foreign scripts unless incorporated in an approved trade name format as set out in the Law on Enterprises and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tên gọi trùng hoặc gần trùng with an existing enterprise name

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where a proposed name is rejected by the Business Registration Office under the Department of Planning and Investment, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the Head of the Business Registration Office within 30 working days of rejection, citing the specific grounds of rejection and providing explanatory memoranda. The appellant may simultaneously submit a revised proposed name that avoids the conflict. An adverse decision on the administrative appeal may be challenged before the provincial People's Court under the Law on Administrative Procedures no later than 30 days after the decision date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only in the form of a licensed virtual-office service provider that maintains a physical, accessible address in Viet Nam, a permanent Vietnamese telephone line, and a mail-relay function registered with the Business Registration Office. The address must not be a common dwelling without a distinguishable physical reception area. For a clinical trial CRO, the Ministry of Health and the Department of Health require substantial local operational presence, including secure document storage, laboratory or file-access facilities, and qualified personnel on site for GCP inspections; therefore a purely virtual office is not accepted for licensure and is not advised.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam (consolidated), particularly Article 22 (registered office), Articles 30-33 (charter capital and capital contribution), Articles 35-42 (enterprise names), Articles 46-66 (multi-member limited liability companies), Articles 73-85 (one-member limited liability companies), and Article 174 (legal representatives); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 37-40 and 58 (investment registration procedures for foreign-invested projects); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration, Articles 21-25 and 44-46; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP on detailed investment procedures, Articles 11-36.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province/city where the registered head office is located; National Enterprise Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) administered by the Business Registration Agency of the Ministry of Planning and Investment
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Enterprise Registration Application Form B-01 (Giay de nghi dang ky doanh nghiep) as prescribed under Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP; for foreign investors, accompanied by the Investment Registration Certificate issued pursuant to Form I-1 and Form I-5 under Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Viet Nam imposes no general statutory minimum charter capital for limited liability companies; however, a foreign-invested clinical-trial CRO project requires the Department of Planning and Investment to appraise the economic justification of the proposed charter capital at the Investment Registration Certificate stage. The subscribed capital must be remitted through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) maintained at a licensed bank in Viet Nam and fully contributed no later than ninety (90) days after issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate. A blocked or escrow deposit account is not statutorily required; the DICA bank statements serve as the evidentiary basis of lawful capital contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE MEMBERS COUNCIL OF [COMPANY NAME] CO., LTD. (FOREIGN-INVESTED LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). DATE: [DD Month YYYY]. VENUE: [Registered Head Office Address, Province/City, Viet Nam]. PRESENT: All founding members/shareholders holding 100 per cent of the charter capital as recorded in Investment Registration Certificate No. [XXX] and Enterprise Registration Certificate No. [XXX]. WHEREAS: (A) The Company was duly incorporated under the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and the Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, with business line ISIC 7490 (contract research organization and clinical-trial management services); (B) the purpose of this first board meeting is to constitute the internal corporate governance required before operational licensing. NOW, THEREFORE, THE MEMBERS COUNCIL UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. 1.1 The charter capital of the Company is fixed at VND [amount] (USD [amount]), allocated among the subscribing members in the proportions stated in the ERC list of members. 1.2 Each member subscribed to and hereby ratifies the allotment of capital as set out in the founding charter; the subscribed capital shall be remitted through the Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) maintained at [bank name] within ninety (90) days from the ERC issuance date, failing which the defaulting member forfeits membership rights in accordance with Article 76 of the Law on Enterprises. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. 2.1 The registered head office situated at [full address] is hereby adopted as the sole statutory seat of the Company, serving as the legal domicile for service of process, tax registration, and State supervision. 2.2 The General Director is authorized to enter into and register leases, environmental registrations, and fire-safety acceptance procedures in respect of that head office. 3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. 3.1 The Members Council appoints: (a) [Full name] as Chairman of the Members Council, with authority to convene member meetings and chair corporate governance; (b) [Full name] as General Director and Legal Representative, with full power for day-to-day management, statutory filings, tax declarations, banking, and personnel administration; (c) [Full name] as Chief Accountant, with responsibility for books of account under the Law on Accounting No. 88/2015/QH13. 3.2 The General Director is directed to: (i) file the Ministry of Health clinical-trial CRO authorization application under Circular 27/2021/TT-BYT; (ii) notify the corporate seal specimen to the National Enterprise Registration Portal; and (iii) open operational bank accounts. 4. EFFECTIVENESS. This First Board Resolution takes effect immediately on signature by all members and shall be annexed to the company charter and the statutory enterprise dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Clearance: Consular Legalization, Apostille, Bilingual Notarization, and Enterprise-Name Availability Vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Legalization and Consular Office; provincial Notary Public Office; National Enterprise Registration Portal (name search module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the foreign founder or shareholder profile for Vietnamese legal effect: (a) obtain an Apostille certificate from the competent authority of the founder's country, or consular legalization where the country is not an Apostille Party; (b) deliver the legalized originals to a licensed notary public for certified Vietnamese translation; (c) complete the enterprise-name availability search on the National Enterprise Registration Portal, confirming that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name under Articles 35-42 of Law No. 59/2020/QH14; (d) reserve at least one alternative name; and (e) execute a notarized power of attorney authorizing the appointed legal counsel or service agent to file the statutory registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Foreign founder's certificate of incorporation or passport (copy)
Apostilled or consular-legalized originals of the founder's constitutive documents
Certified Vietnamese translation executed by a licensed notary public
Alternative name list containing two to three preferred enterprise names
Notarized power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the enterprise name is objected to for similarity, promptly elect the alternative name or file a new name containing a distinct differentiating element; if apostille or legalization is queried, obtain a re-issued apostille from the issuing State and re-notarize the Vietnamese translation; any documentary defect is curable by re-filing without prejudice to the overall timeline.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế), Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam – electronic administration portals: E-Tax (etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) for corporate income tax/VAT filings and payments; E-Invoice Portal (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn) for e-invoice registration, transmission, and certification; enterprise formation via the National Business Registration Portal (Dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) administered by the Ministry of Planning and Investment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Execute corporate authorizations/Power-of-Attorney and certify constituent documents (Charter, legal representative appointment) for the foreign investor. Step 2 — File the investment registration dossier for the foreign-invested LLC (obtain Investment Registration Certificate – IRC) with the provincial Department of Planning and Investment or the export-processing/industrial-zone authority. Step 3 — Concurrently or sequentially file the enterprise registration application for the LLC; upon issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), the enterprise code is automatically granted and, by law, the enterprise code is simultaneously the enterprise's 13-digit tax identification number (Mã số thuế – MST); the applicant does not hold a separate tax-registration step with the tax office. Step 4 — Within 10 working days from the ERC issuance, submit the tax-registration docket (Tax Registration Declaration under Circular 105/2020/TT-BTC) to the managing sub-department of the GDT (typically the Tax Sub-Department of the province/city where the head office is located), covering the legal representative, registered address, bank accounts, authorized signatories, and any dependent branches requiring their own sub-identification numbers. Step 5 — Register the VAT calculation method (credit/deduction method versus direct method), adopt a compliant accounting regime (full regime per Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC or SME regime per Circular 132/2018/TT-BTC), obtain a professional digital-signature certificate and e-invoice solution, and pay the annual business license tax (lệ phí môn bài) within 30 days of ERC issuance (annual rates VND 2,000,000–3,000,000 based on statutory capital).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Vietnamese LLC is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Enterprise Income Tax (CIT, thuế thu nhập doanh nghiệp) at the flat rate of 20% under the Law on Enterprise Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended. There is no transparency or pass-through regime for LLCs: profits and losses are recognized and taxed at the entity level; losses may be carried forward for five years (within 5 consecutive tax years); foreign shareholders are not subject to any Vietnamese dividend withholding tax on after-tax profit remittances, whereas services and royalties paid offshore would be separately scrutinized for foreign-contractor tax and transfer-pricing purposes. Vietnam applies worldwide taxation to resident corporations, subject to foreign tax credit, and therefore the scope is entity-level worldwide income rather than territorial-only taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not operate a check-the-box or partnership pass-through election. Mandatory entity-level taxation is the default for the LLC. Within the statutory framework, the taxpayer may elect: (i) the VAT calculation method (tax-credit/deduction method under Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC versus the direct method), whereby most CRO service providers elect the credit method to preserve input VAT credits/refunds; (ii) the accounting standard (full accounting regime under Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC or SME accounting regime under Circular 132/2018/TT-BTC) if qualifying as a small or medium entity; (iii) the method and scope of transfer-pricing documentation (master file, local file, and Country-by-Country reporting thresholds under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP); and (iv) CIT incentive elections for qualifying high-tech, scientific-research, or innovation activities. No hybrid-mismatch elections are available domestically; Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 132/2020 empower the GDT to disregard or re-characterize hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; thuế giá trị gia tăng – GTGT) administered under the Law on Value Added Tax No. 13/2008/QH12 as amended by Law No. 31/2013/QH14 and guided by Decree 209/2013/ND-CP and Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for the corporate/LLC form: every enterprise with the ERC is automatically and mandatorily VAT-registered at the moment the enterprise code is granted; there is no economic-turnover threshold triggering separate VAT registration for an LLC. (For completeness, a household/individual business may fall outside the VAT net where annual turnover does not exceed VND 100,000,000, but that household exemption does not apply to a foreign-invested LLC.)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing has applied since 1 July 2022 under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Every invoice, including invoices for exported CRO services, must be generated as an electronic invoice in XML format containing the mandatory invoice code, digital signature, and embedded QR code, and must be transmitted to the GDT's E-Invoice Portal (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn). For invoices without pre-assigned tax-authority codes, the e-invoice data must be submitted to the GDT no later than 8 hours from the time the invoice is issued; the system immediately validates the XML/XSD schema and tax-code registry, and invoices that fail validation are rejected, requiring immediate re-issuance. Invoices with pre-assigned tax-authority codes obtain the tax code in real time through the e-invoice portal's web-service API (SOAP/REST), effectively an authorization-clearance step. Export invoices, customs declarations, and VAT refund dossiers are reconciled electronically, and the VNACCS/VCIS customs system applies the same one-stop electronic clearance for any physical goods movement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export services, including contract research organization (CRO)/clinical-trial management services, qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 9 of Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC only if ALL of the following conditions are simultaneously satisfied: (1) the services are supplied to and invoiced to a foreign organization or individual (the foreign sponsor); (2) the foreign sponsor has no permanent establishment or place of business in Vietnam; (3) the services are actually consumed outside Vietnam — for CRO services, the clinical trial data, medical/scientific reports, regulatory dossiers, milestones, and intellectual outputs must be delivered, used, stored, or otherwise enjoyed offshore, while mere local site-monitoring within Vietnam by the Vietnamese CRO will normally be characterized as domestically consumed and exposed to the standard 10% VAT; (4) the services are paid for from abroad in foreign currency through a licensed Vietnamese bank account; and (5) the taxpayer holds the complete documentary evidence bundle described below. Because GDT sub-departments apply a restrictive definition of 'consumed abroad', a CRO must execute a cross-border service agreement with the offshore sponsor and ensure that the contractual and operational substance demonstrates offshore delivery and use of trial results rather than local enjoyment in Vietnam.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed cross-border service/clinical-trial management agreement with the foreign sponsor, indicating scope, milestones, foreign-currency consideration, and governing law
E-invoice with 0% VAT rate issued through the GDT e-invoice portal in statutory XML/QR format
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank statement issued by the Vietnamese commercial bank evidencing receipt of the foreign sponsor's payment from abroad
Foreign sponsor's written certification/receipt confirming that the services were entirely consumed outside Vietnam (offshore use of data, reports, and trial results)

Offshore delivery evidence: accepted milestones, electronic delivery logs, data-transmission records, regulatory filing receipts (e.g., US FDA or EMA submission copies), and correspondence proving the output left Vietnam

For any physical items tied to export (reference standards, biological samples, and trial supplies): Customs Export Declaration (E-Form under VNACCS/VCIS), Air Waybill or Bill of Lading, and packing list
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a historical audit hotspot. A taxpayer who incorrectly claims 0% VAT must re-invoice the service at 10% VAT, is subject to a deficiency assessment with late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and is liable for a penalty of 20% of the under-declared VAT in cases of mistaken declaration, or a penalty between 1 and 3 times the evaded tax where deliberate evasion is established, under Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 125/2020/ND-CP. Retrospective clawback of refunded input VAT with interest is standard when the GDT disallows the offshore-consumption test, and the taxpayer's e-invoice codes may be suspended pending re-moderation. In aggravated cases (fictitious invoices, sham arrangements, documentary fraud, or related-party zero-rating served to shift profits), criminal sanctions for tax evasion apply under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 with fines up to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment from 6 months up to 7 years, in addition to administrative fines, revocation of the enterprise's invoice status, and public blacklisting. The GDT may also adjust transfer prices and impose secondary penalties under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP where the CRO invoices zero-rated services to related offshore sponsors without sufficient substance and comparability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) — Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam, acting under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam (No. 46/2010/QH12) and the Law on Credit Institutions (No. 47/2010/QH12, as amended). The foreign exchange regime is governed by the Foreign Exchange Ordinance (No. 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11, amended by Ordinance 06/2013/UBTVQH13), Decree 70/2014/ND-CP (guidance on the FX Ordinance), and SBV Circulars, notably Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN on foreign exchange transactions between credit institutions and customers (as amended by Circular 11/2022/TT-NHNN). External transactions of foreign-invested enterprises are also supervised by the Ministry of Planning and Investment and the Ministry of Finance for investment registration and tax clearance purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam operates a managed-floating exchange rate regime in which the Vietnamese Dong (VND) is not freely convertible outside the territory. Current-account transactions, including the cross-border export of clinical trial CRO services by a foreign-invested LLC, are fully convertible through SBV-licensed credit institutions, subject to underlying transaction documentation and mandatory statistical purpose codes. Capital-account transactions (initial charter-capital remittance, shareholder loans, capital increases, dividend and profit remittance, transfer of capital/parcels, and residual-asset liquidation transfers) must be settled exclusively via the enterprise's registered Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) under Circular 23/2014/TT-NHNN. Profit remittance is permitted without a lock-up period after the enterprise obtains audited annual financial statements, completes CIT/VAT/final withholding tax obligations, secures tax-clearance confirmation from the competent sub-department of taxation, and passes the bank's documentary checks (board resolution, audited profit distribution statement, corporate governance approval, and proof of no outstanding tax debt). The SBV retains legal authority to impose exchange restrictions or suspend convertibility only in supreme national emergency circumstances pursuant to the FX Ordinance; no such restrictions are currently in force. Practical hurdles for a CRO LLC include the bank's strict verification of the substance behind service-revenue inflows, the reconciliation of each inbound tranche with the 90-day export-proceeds repatriation window, and the requirement that all underlying clinical trial agreements be legally valid under Civil Code obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds arising from the cross-border provision of clinical trial CRO services must be repatriated to a licensed bank in Viet Nam within 90 days of the export date, as required by Article 17 of the Foreign Exchange Ordinance and Article 19 of Decree 70/2014/ND-CP. The proceeds must be credited to the LLC's foreign currency account (FCA) at an SBV-licensed credit institution; receipt through offshore emoney or third-party payment aggregators outside the regulated banking channel is not permitted. Since the 2015 deregulation, there is no mandatory percentage of export proceeds that must be surrendered to the SBV; the enterprise may retain 100% of its export receipts in USD/EUR or convert voluntarily to VND at the negotiating commercial bank's posted exchange rate. The bank will apply the statutory purpose code for 'export of services' and will verify the supporting dossier (cross-border service contract, invoice signed by the foreign sponsor, clinical trial milestones, and the valid VAT e-invoice registration). If repatriation is not completed within the 90-day statutory period, the enterprise must obtain a written extension from the SBV through its advising bank before the deadline; failure to do so subjects the company to administrative fines under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP (sanction framework for monetary and banking violations) and may force mandatory conversion to VND.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for ancillary commercial payments; LOW and NON-COMPLIANT for statutory FDI capital flows and export-proceeds repatriation. Offshore financial technology companies and Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, CurrencyCloud, dLocal, OFX) cannot establish deposit-taking or payment-intermediation activity in Viet Nam without obtaining a licence under the Law on Credit Institutions, Decree 101/2012/ND-CP on non-cash payments (as amended) and SBV Circular 39/2014/TT-NHNN on intermediary payment services. In practice, an offshore EMI may offer collection and settlement facilitation only through a duly licensed Vietnamese partner bank; the EMIC, however, cannot act as the ultimate receiving institution for purpose of the 90-day export-proceeds repatriation rule, and a DICA transaction may never be routed through an EMI. Additional legal constraints: (i) the LLC's capital contribution must be traceable directly from the remitting shareholder to the DICA with the correct statistical purpose code (3211) under Decision 02/2018/QD-NHNN; (ii) SBV foreign-exchange reporting obligations require the receiving licensed bank to identify the cross-border transaction and the true beneficiary of the underlying service contract; (iii) personal-data protection under Decree 13/2023/ND-CP restricts the transfer of clinical-trial-related personal data to offshore payments processors without lawful basis and data-localization safeguards; (iv) unlicensed foreign intermediaries face an absolute legal bar on providing payment intermediation in VND on behalf of Vietnamese residents. A pragmatic compliant architecture is to use a licensed international bank in Viet Nam as the master account bank and to confine EMI rails to non-regulated informational or payroll-ancillary flows only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The physical presence of the Legal Representative (Chairman of the Member's Committee or the General Director) is normally mandatory at the bank branch in Viet Nam for the first KYC interview and biometric verification when opening a corporate account of a foreign-invested LLC. Pure remote/E-KYC onboarding is not available for FDI enterprises: banks may collect documents electronically at the pre-approval stage, but require an in-person visit by a natural person with the statutory representative capacity. If the foreign legal representative is not resident in Viet Nam, the LLC must appoint an onshore authorized signatory via a notarized power of attorney, which must be notarized in the country of origin, apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention (Viet Nam is a contracting party since 1999) or consular-legalized in the absence of apostille, and translated into Vietnamese by an officially recognized translator. The bank will verify the signature specimen, the passport/ID of the authorized representative, and the certificate of the enterprise registration. Some banks, such as HSBC and Vietcombank, permit documentary pre-submission via a secure portal followed by a single branch visit; a few mid-tier banks require two physical visits (account opening and activation). There is no statutory banking regulation permitting fully digital video-verification account opening without the physical presence of a director for foreign-invested entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: multi-tier foreign parent structure, nominee shareholders, or ownership by entities incorporated in low-tax jurisdictions without commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate-chart mapping from the ultimate natural-person controllers (25%+ ownership thresholds) down to the Vietnamese LLC; certificate of incorporation and shareholder registries of each intermediate entity (English translations with legalization); sworn UBO self-declaration under Article 4 of the AML Law 2022; board resolutions approving the Vietnamese investment; local tax registration and prior-year tax returns where available; bank-and-trust reference letters from the parent's principal bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-scope mismatch: clinical trial CRO revenue expected from foreign pharmaceutical sponsors without onshore staff, leases, or evidence of substantive trial activities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master Clinical Trial Service Agreement (CTSA) with the global sponsor; trial-site authorization from the Drug Administration of Viet Nam (DAV) and approval of the Institutional Review Board (IRB); office lease contracts in Viet Nam; labor contracts and social-insurance contribution list of resident staff; investigator sites' statements; project-specific timeline and milestone budget with projected payment dates; redacted subject-informed-consent samples to evidence genuine clinical operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Financing-flow mismatch: charter-capital injection or shareholder-loan inflow in amounts far exceeding the stated capitalization, or remittance from a third party/escrow provider instead of the registered direct investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) reflecting the exact charter-capital amount; capital-contribution schedule signed by the Investor; fund-source documentation (parent audited financial statements, depository certificates for accumulated profits, board-approved investment budget); direct-insurer's undertaking and remittance instruction letter; statutory purpose code 3211 on the SWIFT MT103; any escrow agreements showing the wire chain's origination; certified capitalization memorandum before notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP exposure: adverse media or UBO/PEP screening hits against the legal representative, director, or ultimate beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and PEP screening report (OFAC/EU/UN consolidated lists) from a recognized provider (World-Check, Dow Jones, or the bank's gatekeeper system); an explanation letter with a chronological corporate and transaction history addressing flagged matches; judicial-record certificates and tax-clearance certificates from the jurisdictions of residence of each director/UBO; notarized passport copies; where a PEP match remains, the evidentiary defense must include a board-minuted PEP risk acceptance and a source-of-wealth declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive or mule-account risk: unusual red flags such as demand of multiple accounts ahead of the first trial milestone, frequent changes of ultimate beneficiary, or routing of sponsor fees through unrelated regional payment processors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank's static payment matrix signed by the CFO and the Legal Representative; final treasury-management policy of the CRO LLC; intercompany service description and allocation methodology agreed with the sponsor; letter of undertaking that all cross-border funds will be received directly from the sponsor or named sub-CROs; quarterly business plan integrated with the clinical trial schedule; staged authorization matrix for wire requests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice and documentation hygiene: inability to produce VAT e-invoices or service invoices matching the forecast transaction profile for professional services exports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid tax-invoice serial set registered with the tax authority (e-invoice system eHoadon output); template invoices with proper VAT-inclusive amounts; signed contract annex with milestone-linked invoicing and currency; specimen of the CRO LLC's invoice and the sponsor's purchase-order confirmation; proof of filing of VAT returns and CIT advance payments establishing accounting substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital contributions must be credited to the LLC's registered Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at its principal licensed bank, opened under Circular 23/2014/TT-NHNN concurrently with the issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate. Protocol: (1) the LLC issues a capital-call notice and board resolution stating the amount, currency, and scheduled receipt date; (2) the foreign shareholder's remitting bank transmits the wire via SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 (Remittance Information) quoting the IRC number, the enterprise name, the share-purchase agreement reference, and the explicit purpose 'Contribution to charter capital — direct investment'; (3) the receiving Vietnamese bank assigns the statistical purpose code 3211 (direct investment equity) per Decision 02/2018/QD-NHNN and posts the funds to the DICA in the original foreign currency (USD/EUR) or, upon instruction, converts to VND; (4) the bank files the cross-border foreign-exchange report with the SBV within statutory timelines (daily electronic declaration for the DICA ledger). For operational current-account inflows derived from export of CRO services, the sponsor remits directly to the LLC's operating USD FCA (not the DICA) using the statistical services code for 'other business services' (Group 2 — services, best fit under the SBV code table; the bank must validate the exact sub-code per Decision 02/2018, typically code 225/226 for professional and R&D-business services). The LLC must preserve the service contract, invoice, acceptor's confirmation, and clinical trial progress evidence to support each crediting. Additional verification in practice includes a statement of cash-flow matching against the registered revenue forecast and the attempted confirmation that the remitter is the contracting sponsor and not an unlicensed payment intermediary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound cash-flow rails for the CRO LLC are structured to accommodate: (a) service settlements to offshore sub-CROs, central laboratories, and foreign investigators via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers, each accompanied by a purpose code for import of services, the sub-consulting agreement, invoice, and proof of services rendered (lab report, data transfer certificate, or milestone acceptance); (b) trade-related physical imports (clinical trial consumables, investigational medicinal products, medical devices) via documentary collection or irrevocable commercial letters of credit compliant with UCP 600, advised/confirmed by a Vietnamese LC-issuing bank, together with the import permit from the DAV and customs declaration; (c) intra-group recharge and overhead apportionment via MT103 supported by SG&A allocation memoranda and tax-substantiating records; (d) dividend and profit remittances to the foreign shareholders through the DICA, supported by a board resolution, audited annual financial statements, profit-distribution minutes, and tax-clearance evidence; (e) statutory payments (CIT, VAT, PIT, social insurance) executed through the onshore IBPS/VNDRTGS system and the State Treasury network; and (f) covered FX conversions and forward settlements via the principal bank's e-treasury platform. All outbound SWIFT payments are subject to the bank's financial-crime vetting, with large-value payments requiring an underlying contract/customs declaration, exact purpose-code mapping, and reconciliation against the recognized statistical reporting framework. For payments to high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, enhanced due diligence and an export-control license review are mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/VND foreign-exchange forward contracts, with a maximum tenor of 365 days, permitted onshore under Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN as amended by Circular 11/2022/TT-NHNN, available to corporate clients with a documented underlying transaction (e.g., forecast sponsor fee inflows in USD and forecast sub-CRO payments in USD/VND); collateral or margin may be required by the bank.

FX swaps (USD/VND), including swap-in and swap-out transactions, with a maximum aggregate tenor of 365 days, permissible as an onshore liquidity-management tool to bridge currency mismatches between the DICA/USD FCA position and operational VND expenditure; the underlying transaction must be evidenced for forward leg.

Currency options (USD/VND) with premium paid upfront, permissible under Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN for hedging genuine commercial exposures; the LLC must demonstrate that the notional amount does not exceed the underlying receivables/payables and must obtain internal board approval for option premium expense.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR/VND) available on a bespoke basis for long-dated trial programs, subject to the 365-day tenor cap and bank credit risk approval, executed under ISDA/ISDA-CSA-like Philippine master documentation acceptable to the Vietnamese bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): NOT permissible as an onshore instrument for Vietnamese corporate clients because the SBV regulatory framework requires principal delivery of VND and a demonstrable underlying hedged exposure; offshore USD/VND NDFs are unregulated and unenforceable in the jurisdiction and must be excluded from the treasury policy to avoid breach of the FX Ordinance and Circular 02/2021 rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Declaration (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) where the LLC is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (by 31 March for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine from VND 10,000,000 to VND 15,000,000; continued non-submission may lead to forced dissolution and administrative strike-off from the National Enterprise Registration Database

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Finalisation (Quyết toán thuế năm)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation / provincial tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year (by 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day on outstanding tax; administrative penalties up to VND 25,000,000 for late or false filings; persistent non-compliance triggers enforced tax collection and possible business suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (Báo cáo tài chính đã kiểm toán) submitted to tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation / provincial tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end for tax filing; within 30 days after audit issuance for submission to DPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from VND 5,000,000 to VND 20,000,000 for failure to submit audited financial statements; repeated violations may escalate to tax audit and enterprise compliance review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual investment project implementation report (Báo cáo hoạt động dự án đầu tư)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) or Industrial Zone Authority (if in an export processing zone)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the calendar year, usually on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine from VND 10,000,000 to VND 15,000,000 for late submission; repeated non-compliance may lead to suspension of investment project or revocation of Investment Registration Certificate

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all foreign-invested enterprises (including LLCs) regardless of revenue or asset size; also mandatory if annual revenue exceeds VND 100 billion, total assets exceed VND 50 billion, or if the enterprise operates in a sector requiring audit by law
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) for statutory financial statements; IFRS may be used for consolidated reporting if required by parent or for international financing, subject to approval

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing exists in Vietnam. The LLC must update the register of members within 15 days of any share transfer or capital change and file a change notification to DPI within 30 days. The Annual Enterprise Declaration includes confirmation of members and capital structure, which serves as the annual beneficial ownership confirmation; companies must maintain adequate UBO records for AML compliance but no discrete public UBO register filing is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (standard CIT rate applicable to Vietnamese limited liability companies under Law on Corporate Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12, as amended; effective since 1 January 2016).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying scientific-research and high-technology projects, including contract research/clinical-trial management if certified under the Investment Law, may enjoy a 10% preferential CIT rate for 15 years, followed by a 4-year CIT exemption and 9-year 50% reduction. Manufacturing and high-innovation enterprises in industrial parks/high-tech zones are also eligible for the same incentive window under Government Decree No. 218/2013/ND-CP. A non-incentivized CRO entity remains subject to the standard 20% rate on taxable profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 01/TNDN – Quarterly CIT Provisional Declaration; e-filed via the Vietnam National E-Tax Portal (https://etax.gdt.gov.vn) using a digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter (e.g., 30 April, 30 July, 30 October, 30 January). Quarterly payments must not fall below 80% of the final annual assessed CIT; any shortfall triggers late-payment interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business revenue from clinical trial management services and related commission fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all cross-border sponsor payments in VND at the official exchange rate; the foreign investor does not file this return, the LLC must do so.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses directly attributable to the taxable activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign affiliates must be arm's length and substantiated by invoices/contracts; otherwise they are disallowed.
If Box 03 is negative, carry-forward loss details are referenced; the LLC must attach a schedule for any loss offsets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carried forward from prior years (maximum five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested CROs must use the annual finalization return losses rather than the quarterly return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisionally assessed CIT (taxable income x 20% or applicable incentivized rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay in VND via the e-tax system; wire payments in foreign currency are not accepted for CIT settlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of VND 2,000,000 – VND 4,000,000 if 1–30 days late; VND 4,000,000 – VND 8,000,000 if 30–60 days late; plus 0.03% per day late-payment interest on the unpaid quarterly CIT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02/TNDN – Annual CIT Finalization Return; e-filed via the Vietnam National E-Tax Portal (https://etax.gdt.gov.vn) using a digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 90th day after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by 31 March for a calendar-year entity); the entire remaining CIT liability must be settled by the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer name, tax code, fiscal year, itemized industry code (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541714) and investment certificate reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the foreign shareholder in the appendix; the LLC is the Vietnamese resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue from clinical trial management, protocol design, biometric services, and milestone fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Converted at applicable interbank exchange rate; revenue from outside Vietnam remains taxable if services are performed in Vietnam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable items (e.g., compensation for damages, subsidies not related to business; capital income under treaty exemptions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty-based non-taxability only with TRC and supporting declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Only actual, arm's-length business expenses with lawful invoices; statutory caps (e.g., advertising not exceeding 10% of revenue) apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany fees must comply with transfer pricing guidelines; unexplained payments to foreign related parties are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Breakdown of taxable income subject to 20% standard rate and income eligible for 10%/0% incentive treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incentive claims must be evidenced by an investment registration certificate issued by the management board.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of five-year carried-forward loss applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be continuous; no retroactive amendments allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Definitive CIT due after excluding quarterly provisional payments and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any residual amount before the deadline; excess payments are refundable at the taxpayer's request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual filing: fine up to VND 20,000,000 for delays exceeding 60 days; if the return is not filed within 90 days of the due date, the tax authority may issue an assessment. Late payment interest: 0.03% per day on unpaid CIT. Non-compliance with document requirements triggers additional fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Vietnam imposes no additional dividend withholding tax). After-profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permitted once the LLC has satisfied: (i) payment of all CIT liabilities, (ii) audited annual financial statements, (iii) a shareholder meeting resolution approving the distribution, and (iv) year-end tax finalization. The profit transfer is executed through a licensed Vietnamese bank and reported under Circular 05/2015/TT-BLDTBXH (foreign exchange) – bank will require tax clearance certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because dividends carry no WHT, no treaty relief is required for profit remittance. For interest and royalty payments subject to Foreign Contractor Tax, the beneficial owner should: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the country of residence; (2) submit the standard treaty-relief application to the Vietnamese tax authority via the payer before payment or within the statutory deadline, together with TRC, contract, invoices, and evidence of beneficial ownership; (3) receive the tax authority's notification confirming the reduced or exempt treaty rate; and (4) instruct the payer to withhold at the treaty rate thereafter. This protocol is implemented under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC and the applicable DTA wording.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest on loans from non-residents – 5% effective withholding (CIT component 5%, VAT-exempt); IP royalties to non-residents – 15% aggregate (10% CIT + 5% VAT). Treaty rates: most Vietnamese DTAs reduce interest to 10% (some to 5% for financial institutions in the banking sector) and royalties to 10% (some to 5% for copyright/industrial-property royalties); the reduction is conditional on beneficial ownership and at least a 5-year minimum engagement in Vietnam. If no DTA applies, the domestic FCT rates above prevail.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, a Foreign-Invested LLC is exempt from preparing a Local File and Master File only if its total annual revenue is below VND 200 billion AND the aggregate value of related-party transactions is below VND 30 billion. A Master File is additionally required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue in the preceding fiscal year is at least VND 18,000 billion. A clinical-trial CRO with significant sponsor fees from related multinationals should assume the thresholds are met and maintain contemporaneous TP documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not have a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing substance requirements under Article 47 of Tax Administration Law No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 132/2020/ND-CP demand real economic presence. The CRO must demonstrate actual clinical personnel, premises, functional ownership of trial data, decision-making capability, and risk absorption. Absent these, the tax authority may recharacterize intercompany service fees, deny tax incentives, and impose VAT and CIT adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent CIT Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating clinical-trial service revenue, issuing false invoices, inflating deductible consultancy/foreign data-processing fees, or intentionally failing to file CIT finalization to shift profits overseas.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction up to 2.5 times the amount of evaded tax plus late-payment interest of 0.03%/day; criminal prosecution under Penal Code Art. 200: fine from VND 100 million to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, CFO, and actual managers are jointly liable for the tax arrears; courts may issue civil restitution, impose travel bans (exit visa suspension), and sentence individual wrongdoers to imprisonment where fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a paper CRO with no biostatisticians, no monitored trial sites, no registered premises, or no substantive risk management solely to obtain CIT incentives or funnel royalty/contract fees through a low-tax/no-tax conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR application: recharacterization of the entire arrangement, disallowance of tax incentives, re-assessment of profits, imposition of 20% underpayment penalty, late-payment interest, and administrative fines up to VND 60 million for providing false records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign artificially inflated intercompany contracts or exempt-sale certificates may be personally liable for the recomputed tax, subject to civil damage claims and travel bans; criminal exposure if the shell is used for money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit Local File/Master File/Country-by-Country report within statutory deadlines; using non-arm's-length commission margins for trial-management services; manipulating cost-plus markups; hiding intercompany contracts from the tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment to taxable income plus 20% penalty on the under-declared tax; separate penalty of VND 5–25 million for non-submission of TP documents; if intentional, the fine rises to 2.5 times the evaded tax and the matter may be referred for criminal tax investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for TP policy are liable for the adjusted CIT and penalties; they can be held jointly and severally for misleading the tax authority; travel restrictions may apply until the entire TP debt and penal interest is settled.
